resources.string: Low-entropy sources; short key lengths; deprecated algorithms; plaintext key export; missing hardware-backing or broad key purpose.
AES-256 key generated via Android Keystore. 256-bit key, hardware-backed, never leaves the TEE.
DES key generated — only 56 effective bits. NIST has disallowed DES since 2005. Brute-forceable in hours.
Key exported using Android Keystore key wrapping. Key material encrypted before it leaves the secure environment.
AES key exported as raw bytes to a file. Anyone with file access has the key — all encrypted data compromised.
Key generated with setKeyPurposes(ENCRYPT_DECRYPT) only. Cannot be misused for signing or key agreement.
Key generated with KeyPurpose.ENCRYPT_DECRYPT and SIGN — one key for all operations. Violates least-privilege principle.
AES-256 key generated by KeyGenerator backed by OS CSPRNG. Full 256-bit entropy guaranteed.
AES key derived from device IMEI (15 digits = ~50 bits entropy). Brute-force space far smaller than 128-bit key.
2048-bit RSA key. Meets current NIST recommendations. Infeasible to factor with foreseeable computing resources.
512-bit RSA key generated. Factorable with public resources. All data encrypted with it is compromised.
